**Finding [high, test_coverage] (codex-auditor-F004-i1, sole finding)** — "`test_event_copy_brief_fields.py` remains untracked, so it would be absent from a committed patch or fresh checkout." The file's contents were correct and complete; the defect was purely that it had never been added to the index, so `git ls-files` rejected it and it showed as `??`. I staged it with `git add`, and confirmed the fix by `git ls-files --error-unmatch` now resolving the path and `git status --porcelain` reporting it as `A` rather than `??`. Because the auditor's concern was patch completeness — that the submitted change be self-contained on a fresh checkout — I also staged the rest of the F004 change set that the test exercises: `event_copy.py`, `operator_console.py`, and the 16 `event_messaging_snapshots/*.json` fixtures whose `plain_consequence` values changed from the aliased detail string to `null` as a direct consequence of removing the aliasing. The staged patch is now 19 files, 520 insertions. Verification: the required file passes 56/56; combined with the pre-existing `test_event_copy_f001.py` RenderedEvent contract, 76/76; and the snapshot/sanitization suites covering the staged fixtures, 85/85. `git diff --cached --check` is clean. No implementation logic changed this iteration — the four acceptance criteria were already satisfied and remain so.
